correctness.rationale: The independent-digit Fourier transform is the product of Bernoulli factors. Each factor has a strict minimum at the two odd-root phases adjacent to -1, i.e. 4k=+/-1 mod b^j; the two solutions mod b^m simultaneously minimize every factor, and minimizing the largest-level factor forces this equality set. Positivity and strictness use 0<w_j<1; b odd makes 4 invertible. Gram eigenvalues are 1+/-|hat nu|. Fair-bias sine products and nonfair products have convergent log corrections. Independent raw discrete Fourier enumeration verified both minimum and equality residues in 18 configurations b=3,5,7 and m=1,2,3 with fair and varying biased weights; infinite-level rate is proved by convergent products, not the bounded tests.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The infinite no-frame theorem concerns existence of an exponential frame, not exact finite two-character coherence. The digit-tower result concerns a different full-frame determinant; no dominating all-bias minimum is established by their accessible statements.
